comments.author: @guitarsoundsaround
comments.text: They are crooks! And very wealthy. Don’t be fooled.

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Some colonies certainly control substantial assets, but that’s different from individual Hutterites personally owning that wealth. And I wouldn’t label an entire community “crooks” without specific evidence. The whole reason I made the video was to look at both how successful the system can be and the criticisms of how it works.

comments.author: @x45667xf
comments.text: Yeah those are called Hutterite colonies.

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Yep! Hutterite colonies. What fascinated me was what happens once you look past the name and into how the colonies actually work and own everything collectively. It’s a pretty remarkable system.

replies.author: @Yourmomma568
replies.text: ​@HiddenCanadahow is that any different from communism? Do you think that communists don't engage in market exchange?

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Not quite 😄 Hutterites practice communal ownership within their colony, but they still run businesses, sell products in the market and compete like other farms. It’s a pretty unusual mix of communal living and capitalism, which is part of what makes them so interesting.

comments.author: @Cacatoes1
comments.text: How do you become a Hutterite

replies.author: @x45667xf
replies.text: Hutterites are a extremely hard working society. You would have to give up everything in your current life. If you're female you will be treated as a lesser being. Something as simple as going to Value Village to buy a pair of socks will be the highlight of your month. Some colonies try to branch out and be apart of the broader community. Some colonies are very closed off and aren't welcoming to outsiders. I live in Manitoba and I actually go to many colonies for work reasons.

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: You actually can, although it’s pretty rare for outsiders. You’d generally have to live on a colony for a while, accept the Hutterite faith and communal way of life, and go through a probation period. If everything works out, adult baptism is what officially makes you a full member.

comments.author: @dennisnsharleneparker9797
comments.text: You have done a lot of research and built a comprehensive and informative video.  Good job.  Some of the challenges when discussing topics like this is remaining objective and free from envy.

replies.author: @dennisnsharleneparker9797
replies.text: @HiddenCanada My limited interaction with the Hutterite community while living in Lethbridge AB in the '60s and '70s, has shown me that corruption, selfishness, immorality or the desire for pre-eminence are not the exclusive domain of any race, culture or religious denomination. In the absence of these things, I can see a communal society such as these folk as being a happy and prosperous environment "if one does not mind giving away personal autonomy".

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Thank you, I really appreciate that. That was one of the harder parts of researching this, there are things about the system that clearly work very well, and there are also legitimate criticisms and trade-offs. I tried to show both without turning it into either praise or condemnation.
